chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about mentioning a Chapter from the Book to supplicate with during the prayer, such as 'Say: He is Allah, One', so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are supplicating with it, there is no problem.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite Quranic chapters as supplication during prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of treating Quranic recitation, specifically Surah Al-Ikhlas, as a suppension (du'a) during prayer, highlighting the fluidity between recitation and invocation in Shia jurisprudence. This permissibility underscores the spiritual depth of the Quranic text, where its words serve not only as divine command but also as a direct medium for communicating with God. The ruling reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the versatility of Quranic verses in personal devotion and ritual worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about mentioning the Chapter from the Book to supplicate with during the Salāt, like [112:1] Say: He Allah is One (Chapter 112)’. So heasws said: ‘When you were supplicating by it, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about reading a chapter of the book in the form of an appeal for help in Salah (prayer) like Chapter 112. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you read it in the form of appeal for help it is not harmful.’”
